annotations.annotation_text: Page 489 opens Book 3, Chapter 3 ("The Inquest of Yawn") during the Age of Men phase. This passage continues the judicial inquest over the prostrate body of Yawn (Shaun), voices of the dead rising through him, HCE's final confession, featuring Yawn/Shaun, Mamalujo, HCE (voice), ALP (voice). The nocturnal dream-narrative layers Dublin topography, world mythology, and linguistic alchemy into polysemic prose.
sources: Campbell, Joseph and Robinson, Henry Morton. A Skeleton Key to Finnegans Wake. https://archive.org/details/skeletonkeytofin00camp
McHugh, Roland. Annotations to Finnegans Wake. https://archive.org/details/annotationstofin0000mchu_h5g8
Gordon, John. Finnegans Wake: A Plot Summary. https://johngordonfinnegan.weebly.com
JJDA: Finnegans Wake Genetic Edition. https://jjda.ie

annotations.annotation_text: Mid-page polysemic node on page 489 ("The Inquest of Yawn"): Joyce weaves multilingual puns across 60+ languages — etymological roots from the Contemporary Literature Press lexicons (Romanian, Scandinavian, Slavic, Classical) intersect with local Dublin speech rhythms. The Age of Men dream-logic transforms ordinary syntax into a palimpsest of global literary and mythic references.
sources: Tindall, William York. A Reader's Guide to Finnegans Wake. https://archive.org/details/readersguidetofi00tind
Contemporary Literature Press: Multilingual Lexicons for FW. https://editura.mttlc.ro
Atherton, James S. The Books at the Wake. https://archive.org/details/booksatwake0000athe

annotations.annotation_text: The Letter motif "letter" on page 489 ("The Inquest of Yawn"): ALP's mysterious document — scratched from the midden by Biddy Doran the Hen — represents the genesis of all writing within the judicial inquest over the prostrate body of Yawn (Shaun), voices of the dead rising through him, HCE's final confession. During this Age of Men phase, the letter functions simultaneously as archaeological artifact, love note, legal deposition, and the text of Finnegans Wake itself.
sources: Bishop, John. Joyce's Book of the Dark. https://archive.org/details/joycesbookofdark0000bish
Deane, Vincent, et al. The Finnegans Wake Notebooks at Buffalo. https://www.brepols.net
